# Scaffold

## Why this session exists

Move from single-shot interpretation to population-level tokamak physics.

::: {.notes}
[scaffold]

This deck is a scaffold, like its notebook. Session 06 closes the course by
changing the unit of analysis from one discharge to a campaign.
:::

## Session workflow

summary table $\rightarrow$ filtering and limits $\rightarrow$ regression or
classification $\rightarrow$ physical claim

::: {.notes}
[scaffold]

The open question for this session is data. Three shots are packaged; real
operational-space work needs the database, and HSDS access is not part of the
offline contract. Whoever writes it has to decide whether the session teaches
the method on three shots or requires lab mode.
:::

## Practice goal

Make a claim about a population of discharges that survives its own filtering.

::: {.notes}
[scaffold]

The teaching risk here is selection effects: a limit found after filtering the
population is a property of the filter as much as of the machine.
:::
